summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, esophageal varices, and recent bladder tumor resection was admitted for evaluation of hematuria, gastrointestinal bleeding, and abdominal pain. He had a markedly elevated PSA of 99.2, prompting urology consultation and plans for a bone scan and outpatient initiation of casodex for suspected prostate cancer. During the hospitalization, he developed nausea and vomiting, which resolved after discontinuation of casodex and oxycodone, suggesting medication-related side effects. His renal function showed transient worsening, likely pre-renal due to dehydration, which improved with fluids. Imaging revealed mild colonic wall thickening consistent with chronic colopathy and a left ureteral stent without hydronephrosis. No active GI bleeding was observed during admission, and hemoglobin remained stable. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged in urology and gastroenterology, and instructions to monitor kidney function and resume home medications.
